findings.title: isinstance check makes kill() a no-op for real flusher processes
findings.body: `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is never true for the processes this class creates. `self.mp_context` is the 'spawn' context, whose `Process` is `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. That class derives from `BaseProcess`, not from `multiprocessing.context.Process`, so the check is False and `process.kill()` is skipped. Before this PR the code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (catching only ValueError), so this is a regression. Consequence: when a flusher is hung (alive but `process_healthy_since` is stale), it is never killed. `_create_process_for_shards` then starts a second process for the same shards while the hung one keeps flushing the same Redis segments. That can produce duplicate segments to buffered-segments and leaks a live process on every restart. Only the thread path (used in tests) reaches the guarded code, so the tests do not catch this. Fix by testing against `BaseProcess` or by checking `hasattr(process, 'kill')`.

findings.title: join() never terminates spawned flusher processes on timeout
findings.body: The termination in `join` uses `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, which is False for `SpawnProcess` objects (see the same check in `_ensure_processes_alive`). So after the deadline passes, no flusher process is terminated. They are daemon processes, so they keep running until interpreter exit, possibly still flushing to Redis and producing to Kafka after the consumer has shut down and its shards may have been reassigned. This code was already broken before this PR. The PR rewrote this loop to cover all processes and kept the broken check, so it should be fixed in the same change.

findings.title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op, so the test still races
findings.body: The test starts with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which patches `time.sleep` for the whole process. The `time.sleep(0.1)` added at line 62 therefore does nothing, although the comment says it gives flusher threads time to observe the drift change. The test still depends on the flusher thread running a flush iteration with drift 9000 before `step.join()` sets `stopped`. If it doesn't, `messages` is empty and `(msg,) = messages` fails. The test is flaky as written. Wait for the message to appear (e.g. poll with a deadline), or capture a real sleep before patching.

findings.title: wait_produce metric uses tag key 'shards' while all other flusher metrics use 'shard'
findings.body: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses the tag key `shards`. The produce timer and segment_size metric in the same function, and flusher_unhealthy, all use `shard`. Dashboards or monitors that group by `shard` will not match this series, and the naming is inconsistent within a single change.

findings.title: Docstring says one process per shard, but the defaults do not
findings.body: The class docstring says the flusher 'Creates one process per shard'. The consumer's `--flusher-processes` option defaults to 1, so production runs one flusher for all shards. The factory default of None gives one process per shard. The `max_processes` cap also limits the count. The documentation does not describe these defaults, and the consumer default contradicts the PR description's 'a process per redis shard'.

findings.title: Unused _create_process_for_shard duplicates a similarly named method
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is never called. The code calls `_create_process_for_shards` (plural) instead. Two near-identical method names that do different things are a maintenance hazard. Remove the dead method.

findings.title: Negative --flusher-processes crashes startup with KeyError
findings.body: `flusher_processes` is passed through with no validation. A negative value makes `self.num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards))` negative, so `process_to_shards_map` is empty. The loop then does `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]`, which raises KeyError during consumer startup with an unhelpful message. A value of 0 silently falls back to one process per shard. Validate the option (minimum of 1) in the CLI definition or in the constructor.
